Internal Setup Guide

Connecting SIQ Code + Claude
via VS Code

A step-by-step walkthrough for wiring the SIQ codebase to Claude inside VS Code — from environment setup to first successful connection.

SIQ
codebase
VS
VS Code
C
Claude

Software needs

VS Code latest version, installed and signed in
Claude Desktop paid plan required
1

Get repo access to zoholivesupport SIQ

Before anything else, request access to the zoholivesupport repository from the dev team. This is the SIQ codebase Claude will be reading and working in, so the whole setup is blocked until access is granted.

! Access approval can take time — request this first so it isn't the bottleneck later in the guide.
2

Create a new branch for your purpose SIQ

Once access is granted, open the zoholivesupport repo at repository.zohocorpcloud.in/zohocorp/zohosalesiq/zoholivesupport. Work happens off a dedicated branch, not directly on DEV_MASTER, so create one before making any changes.

zoholivesupport > Files — New (top right) > This branch > New Branch

How to navigate there:

Files tab (left sidebar)
  → confirm base branch selector reads "DEV_MASTER" (top-left dropdown)
  → click the teal "New" button (top-right of the file explorer toolbar)
  → in the dropdown, under "This branch"
  → select "New Branch"

Name the branch after what you're doing (feature, fix, or your username), then create it off DEV_MASTER.

In the New Branch form that opens:

Branch Type   → None
Branch Name   → your branch name (e.g. PM_USE)
Create From   → DEV_MASTER
Notify Users  → optional

New Branch form — set Branch Name, keep Create From as DEV_MASTER, then click Create

i Once you hit Create, the new branch is cloned from DEV_MASTER and takes on the branch name you entered. That branch is now your working branch for the rest of this setup.
! The "New" dropdown has two sections — "This directory" (files/folders) and "This branch" (branch/release actions). Make sure you're clicking "New Branch" under "This branch", not "New File" under "This directory".
3

Switch to your new branch SIQ

After creation, you'll usually be navigated to the new branch automatically. If not, switch to it manually via the branch dropdown (top-left, where it currently shows "DEV_MASTER"). 

Branch dropdown (top-left, shows current branch)
  → click to open
  → "Branches" tab
  → type your branch name in the search box
  → select it from the matching results

Branch dropdown → Branches tab → search box → select your branch from the results

! The search is a partial match, so typing part of your branch name is enough to filter the list down.
4

Get the code into VS Code VS Code

Click the Code button (top right of the repo view) to open the clone panel.

Code (top right) — clone URL, branch clone command, and open-with options

Two ways to get the files:

Easy way   → "Download Source Code As" → ZIP → open the folder in VS Code
Hard way   → copy "Branch Clone Command" → git clone in a terminal
! The easy way (ZIP) is quick, but the con is you can't pull future changes into it — it's a one-time snapshot, not a live clone.

For a proper working copy that stays in sync, go the harder route: copy the Branch Clone Command shown in the panel above (it already points at your branch) and use it to clone via git.

5

Clone the branch in a terminal VS Code

Open Terminal, navigate to any folder where you'd like the project to live, create a new folder for it, then paste the Branch Clone Command you copied in Step 4. (Cloning can take a few minutes depending on your connection and the repo size — just let it run.) 

cd Documents/          # or any location you prefer
mkdir SIQ-Code
cd SIQ-Code
git clone https://zrepository.zohocorpcloud.in/zohocorp/zohosalesiq/zoholivesupport.git -b YOUR_BRANCH_NAME
# (the git clone line is the Branch Clone Command you copied in Step 4)

Git will prompt for credentials — enter your Zoho username, then your password (or access token) when asked. 

Username for 'https://zrepository.zohocorpcloud.in': your.username
Password for 'https://your.username@zrepository.zohocorpcloud.in': ••••••••

Not sure of your username? Find it on the repo page: top-right profile picture → My Profile → Username.

Terminal — create folder, clone the branch directly, authenticate

! The -b YOUR_BRANCH_NAME flag clones straight into that branch — replace it with the branch name you created in Step 2.
6

Open in VS Code VS Code

Launch VS Code. If this is your first time using it, sign up / sign in with your account so extensions and settings sync properly.

Then open the cloned repo as a folder — not a single file — so VS Code loads the full project structure and git context. There are two ways to do this: 

Option A — from within VS Code
File → Open Folder…
  → navigate to Documents/SIQ-Code/zoholivesupport
  → select the folder → Open

Option B — from the terminal
cd Documents/SIQ-Code/zoholivesupport
code .

Either way, VS Code reloads with the file explorer on the left showing the repo's folders (.claude, build, source, and so on) — confirming the whole project is open, not just a piece of it.

! Open the top-level zoholivesupport folder, not a subfolder inside it — Claude and VS Code both need the full repo root to work correctly.
7

Install the Claude Code extension Claude

With the zoholivesupport folder open, install the official Anthropic extension that brings Claude Code into VS Code. 

Extensions icon (left sidebar) or Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + X
  → search "Claude Code"
  → select "Claude Code for VS Code" (publisher: Anthropic)
  → Install

Extensions → Claude Code for VS Code (Anthropic) — shows as installed once done

Authorize your account:

Open the Claude icon in the sidebar (or Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + P → "Claude Code: Login")
  → this opens a browser tab for sign-in
  → log in with your Claude account (paid plan required — see Step 0)
  → click Allow / Authorize when prompted
  → return to VS Code — the panel now shows you as connected
! Authorization uses your Claude account, not your Zoho login. Use the same paid-plan account listed in the "Software needs" section up top.
8

Install packages in the v3 folder VS Code

Open VS Code's built-in terminal and navigate into the v3 project folder to install its dependencies. 

Shortcut (Mac & Windows)   → Ctrl + `  (backtick)
Manual                     → View → Terminal
                              or Terminal → New Terminal

Then, from the repo root:

cd webapps/V3
npm i

Terminal → cd into v3 → npm i — wait for it to finish before moving on

This pulls in all the packages the v3 project depends on. Like the clone in Step 5, this can take a few minutes — let it finish before opening or running anything.

! Run npm i again every time you start working in v3, not just the first time. It keeps your local packages in sync with whatever's changed in package.json.
9

Install the local SSL certificate VS Code

Before running the project, a local key certificate needs to be trusted on your machine so the app can run over HTTPS locally. A browser extension step follows separately — this step covers the certificate only. 

Download: workdrive.zohoexternal.in — localhost.pem

Then, in Terminal, trust it against your system keychain:

sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain ~/Downloads/localhost.pem

Replace ~/Downloads/localhost.pem with the actual path and filename of the certificate you just downloaded — it won't always land in Downloads.

! This command needs admin access on your machine — sudo will prompt for your local admin password. Without it, the certificate won't be trusted and the app won't load correctly over HTTPS.
10

Install the browser extension SIQ

Open the salesiq-redirector repo and download it as a ZIP, the same way you did for the main codebase in Step 4. 

https://repository.zohocorpcloud.in/zohocorp/zohosalesiq/salesiq-redirector

  → top right corner → Code → Download Source Code As → ZIP

Unzip it and keep the folder somewhere you won't accidentally delete — Chrome will load the extension directly from this folder, not from the ZIP.

Then, in Chrome:

chrome://extensions/
  → toggle "Developer mode" on (top right)
  → Load unpacked
  → select the unzipped salesiq-redirector folder
  → enable the extension's toggle once it appears in the list

chrome://extensions/ — Developer mode on, then Load unpacked

! If you move or delete the unzipped folder later, Chrome will disable the extension automatically — keep it in a stable location.
11

Start the local server VS Code

Back in the terminal, inside v3, run npm i once more — same as Step 8, just to make sure everything's current before starting the server — then start it up. 

cd webapps/V3
npm i
npm run dev

This takes a few seconds to spin up. Once it's done, you're set — continue using your local account exactly as before, at: 

salesiq.localzoho.com
! Infrastructure's done here — SIQ codebase, VS Code, Claude Code, and the local certificate and extension are all in place. One step left: actually working with Claude.
12

Talk to Claude Claude

With the dev server running, ask Claude to read the codebase and start working — reviewing a file, tracing a bug, making a change, whatever you need.

Every change Claude makes is reflected instantly in your local view — the dev server hot-reloads as files are saved, so you'll see the result right away in the browser. Server-side data behaves exactly the same as it does when you're working locally without Claude, so nothing about your usual local workflow changes.

! You're fully set up. Point Claude at the repo, describe what you need, and watch it show up live in the browser.
